France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
November 16, 2026
Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.
French federation chief Philippe Diallo was "unanimously" backed by UEFA to be a candidate in FIFA's presidential election, which will take place in March in Morocco, with criticism against current chiefGianni Infantino growing.
European football's governing body said it has backed Diallo "unanimously" in a bid to replace Infantino, with UEFA's "full support" behind the Frenchman.
Veteran Japanese official Kohzo Tashima has also announced his candidacy, with the deadline for candidates to stand for election being November 18.
Potential candidates for the post must show letters of support of five of FIFA's 211 member associations, before going through eligibility and integrity checks.
Son of boxer, head of French football
Diallo, the 63-year-old head of the French Football Federation (FFF), is the son of a Senegalese boxing champion.
He was appointed as FFF president in 2023 after being elected with a large majority. He was reelected in 2024 for another four-year term.
Back in September, Diallo said the FFF withdrew its support of Infantino ahead of the March 2027 election, saying the trust in the FIFA President "has been betrayed."
"The way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us," the French football head said about the decision.
The Frenchman could become FIFA's first black president, while also being the organization's third head from France, after first president Robert Guerin and third president Jules Rimet.
Embattled Infantino
Gianni Infantino has been in charge of world football's governing body since 2016.
He has been facing growing criticism since his plan of selling parts of the World Cup to private investors. The criticisms were led by UEFA and its President Aleksander Ceferin.
Infantino ended up scrapping the plan, but UEFA went ahead and took FIFA to court in the US trying to gather evidence, ahead of potentially complaining to Swiss authorities about alleged "criminal mismanagement" by Infantino.
FIFA's headquarters are located in Zürich, Switzerland.
Infantino was also criticized after creating a peace prize and awarding it to US President Donald Trump last year.
The connection between Infantino and Trump came under criticism once again during the World Cup, after United States forward Folarin Balogun was allowed to take part in the round of 16 game against Belgium despite being shown a red card in the previous game.
The US president admitted to having personally intervened through a conversation with Infantino.
